title: kbgit.py publish lets a noreply or no-reply local part at any domain, and any host whose first label is noreply, through its message guard
goal: publish's message guard passes a noreply address only at the domains the kb names (the Claude Code trailer's and users.noreply.github.com) and the placeholder domains, and refuses a noreply or no-reply local part at any other domain and a host whose first label is noreply

run:
import os, subprocess, sys, tempfile
sys.path.insert(0, "_tools"); import kbpublic
d = tempfile.mkdtemp(); e = dict(os.environ, GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=os.devnull, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM="1", GIT_AUTHOR_NAME="t", GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL="t@example.com", GIT_COMMITTER_NAME="t", GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL="t@example.com")
g = lambda *a: subprocess.run(["git", *a], cwd=d, env=e, check=True, capture_output=True)
g("init", "-q")
bad = ["noreply" + chr(64) + "gmail.com", "no-reply" + chr(64) + "corp-mail.test", "jan" + chr(64) + "noreply.corp-mail.test"]
miss = []
for a in bad:
    g("commit", "-q", "--allow-empty", "-m", "docs: x\n\nReviewed-by: " + a)
    if not kbpublic.message_refusals("HEAD", "HEAD~1" if a != bad[0] else None, {}, d):
        miss.append(a.split(chr(64))[0] + " at " + a.split(chr(64))[1].split(".")[0])
print("not refused: " + ", ".join(miss) if miss else "ok"); sys.exit(1 if miss else 0)
